request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Patient Name: N/A
Medical Record Number: N/A
Date of Admission: N/A
Date of Discharge: N/A
Date of Dictation: [DATE]

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient was admitted to our university hospital with a sudden severe headache in the forehead. Brain computed tomography (CT) revealed a large epidural hematoma in the right frontal lobe with midline shift. The patient had no past history of trauma or cardiovascular risk factors, including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking, diabetes mellitus, collagen diseases, alcoholism, and drug abuse.
DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
TREATMENT:
The patient discontinued fingolimod and a month later the lymphopenia had resolved, but the hematoma showed no improvement. Therefore, a direct evacuation was performed, and a 12 g organized hematoma was successfully removed. After the operation, the patient received a single course of methylprednisolone pulse therapy (1 g/day for 3 successive days) followed by treatment with dimethyl fumarate instead of fingolimod. The patient showed no recurrence of hematoma or bleeding for more than a year.

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient is advised to follow up with their physician for further evaluation and management of their RRMS. No additional concerns were noted.

DISCHARGE CONDITION:
Stable and improved.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The case describes a spontaneous (non-traumatic) epidural hematoma in a patient with relapsing-remitting MS on fingolimod, who also developed lymphopenia. The hematoma was the reason for admission and was treated surgically.

In ICD-10-AM, a traumatic epidural hematoma is coded to S06.4. This patient had no history of trauma, so the hematoma is non-traumatic. A non-traumatic extradural hemorrhage is coded to G93.8 (other specified disorders of brain), or in older versions to G95.1 or I62.1. ICD-10 category I62.1 is "Nontraumatic extradural haemorrhage", which fits best.

I62 is therefore the most specific category for a non-traumatic extradural hemorrhage.

CODE: I62
